title: Declarative JSON contract injection fuzz suite for streaming+toolcalls
creator: Priya Shah
description: Purpose: Build a reproducible, declarative fuzz test harness that injects contract deviations into streaming responses and interleaved tool/function-calls to validate JSON mode enforcement and constrained-decoder recovery paths across runtime variants. Scope: streaming responses (partial chunks, truncated frames), interleaved toolcall outputs, KV/prefix cache warm/cold states, and compatibility across hosted/dedicated/private deployments. Deliverable: a runnable suite that outputs per-test verdicts, failure traces, and a canonicalized diff of model output vs expected schema; integration with CI to block merges on regressions above the threshold.
acceptance_criteria: Declarative test spec format (YAML/JSON) for describing injection patterns and expected schema assertions
Fuzz harness can simulate: chunk boundary splits, truncated UTF-8 sequences, extra tokens before/after JSON root, and interleaved 'tool' messages that include JSON payloads
End-to-end runs across three runtime profiles: hosted-api, dedicated-pool, private-vpc with identical test vectors
Failure classification produced: parse-failure, schema-violation, toolcall-corruption, fallback-triggered
Automated report posted to dashboard with historical trends and PR-level badge if regression detected
test_plan: 1) Implement declarative spec parser and mutation engine. 2) Build streaming client that can replay sequences with controlled chunk sizes and intentional mid-token splits. 3) Implement toolcall interleaving simulator that emits tool result events both before and after partial JSON payloads. 4) Wire constrained-decoder knobs: token blocking lists, top_k/top_p sweeps, temperature variations, and backoff policies. 5) Run matrix across model family variants (open-llama-13b-quant, rdw-base-7b, rdw-compat-1.0) and runtime kernels (fast-attn, fallback-generic). 6) Collect metrics: schema_failure_rate, mean_time_to_detect, false_positive_rate for sentinel detection. 7) Add CI job gating on schema_failure_rate <= 0.5% for release branch. Test artifacts and canonical failures are stored at the test-run bucket for triage.
updates: 2025-11-05 - Triage: initial spec drafted by Priya. Identified need to reuse the streaming client harness from ENG-14266.

2025-11-07 - Spike complete: mutation engine prototype that injects mid-token splits and extra closing braces. Found current constrained-decoder backoff isn't invoked when toolcall event precedes EOF. Filing follow-up task for runtime routing fix.

2025-11-09 - Design review with runtime team. Decision: implement parser-level sentinel detection AND model-level constrained decoding to reduce flaky failure modes. Trade-off: small perf overhead on streaming path when sentinel verification enabled; mitigated by sampling/flag per-route.

2025-11-11 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-runtime/pull/1267 (fuzz harness + spec parser). Initial unit tests green; integration tests failing on one dedicated pool profile due to KV cache interaction. Assigned to Daniel to debug cache TTL collision.
2025-11-12 - Added opt-in route flag for 'declarative-contract-validation' to avoid perf regression on routes that don't need strict enforcement. Next: add historical dashboard and CI gating.
notes: Primarily aimed at preventing regressions introduced by kernel changes and streaming parser optimizations.
We should coordinate with SDK team to produce client-side test runners for similar fuzz vectors so customers can reproduce failures locally.
Consider adding a lighter-weight sampler that runs in production (1% of traffic) to detect emergent schema drift without full contract validation overhead.
